    11→- **Austin Strategic Mobility Plan (ASMP)** — Street Network Table and Bicycle Priority Network (`atd.knack.com/asmp`). Assigns every street a Street Level (0–5) and a target ROW width from centerline. ASMP supersedes the legacy AMATP.

    13→- **Transportation Criteria Manual (TCM)** — Section 2 (street design), 3 (intersections), 4 (sidewalks), 5 (bicycle facilities), 7 (driveways), 8 (TCP), 9 (parking / bus stops), 10 (TIA process and Table 10-6 nexus standards).
    14→- **TIA Guidelines** — Sections 2 (determination), 4 (scope), 5 (sub-threshold), 6 (compliance), 7 (NTA).
    15→- **TxDOT roadway inventory** — for ASMP Level 5 streets (freeways/interstates) and any IH/US/SH-prefixed roadway. Surveyor tool: `txdot_roadway_lookup` (functional class, lanes, AADT).
    16→- **Scenic Roadway designations** — LDC § 25-10-7 (the 23 enumerated scenic roadways) and LDC § 25-10-81(3) (Scenic Roadway Sign District). Note: the scenic roadway *sign* district is in Ch. 25-10; Hill Country Roadway *development* rules are at LDC §§ 25-2-1025 and 25-2-1127.
    17→- **Project Connect System Plan map** — Orange Line and other rail corridors. Not codified in Bureau; published by ATD/CapMetro.
    18→
    19→## Regulatory pathway
    20→
    21→| Trigger | Path | Typical timeline |
    22→|---|---|---|
    23→| Any new development on a street in the ASMP Street Network | TIA Determination Worksheet through TDS portal, signed by TDS Lead Development Review Engineer | 2–6 weeks |
    24→| < 2,000 unadjusted daily trips | No TIA; sub-threshold mitigation may still apply (LDC § 25-6-101(B)) | concurrent with site plan |
    25→| 2,000–4,999 unadjusted daily trips | Transportation Assessment + TDM Plan; TDS-approved scope first | 4–6 months end-to-end |
    26→| ≥ 5,000 unadjusted daily trips | Full TIA + TDM Plan; TDS-approved scope first | 6–9 months end-to-end |
    27→| Residential street access AND ≥ 300 net new daily trips (or any public K-12 school) | Neighborhood Traffic Analysis (NTA) — TDS staff write the memo; applicant submits 24-hr tube counts | 2–4 months |
    28→| Street frontage on ASMP-designated street | ROW dedication (street deed or plat); City-issued proportionality memo required under § 25-6-23 | recordation before site plan approval |
    29→| TxDOT-maintained frontage (IH, US, SH, Level 5) | TxDOT coordination letter / Approval Block; alignment set by TxDOT | additive 2–6 months |
    30→| Frontage on Hill Country Roadway corridor | Hill Country Roadway development standards (LDC § 25-2 Subchapter C) overlay | concurrent with site plan |
    31→| Site within 200 ft of any of the 23 Scenic Roadways OR 1,000 ft of a Hill Country Roadway | Scenic Roadway Sign District (LDC § 25-10-124) governs signage | concurrent with site plan |
    32→| Site within an adopted regulating plan (NBG, ERC, MLK TOD, Plaza Saltillo, Lamar/Justin Lane) | Future street extension + frontage standards apply even before street is built | concurrent with site plan |
    33→| Site along plausible Project Connect Orange Line alignment | Flag for ROW reservation up to 65 ft from centerline (130 ft total) — verify externally | additive coordination |
    34→
    35→## Constraints to evaluate
    36→
    37→### ROW dedication (existing vs. future)
    38→
    39→- **Existing vs. future ROW is the single most important distinction.** Survey-confirmed existing ROW often differs from ASMP target width. Build-out massing and setback geometry must be measured from the *future* (ASMP) ROW line, not the curb or existing property line (LDC § 25-6-54(D)).
    40→- Look up each frontage in the ASMP Street Network Table (`atd.knack.com/asmp`). Document Street Level (0–5) and target half-width.
    41→  - Level 0 = alleys; Level 1 = local/residential collectors; Level 2 = collectors; Level 3 = minor/major arterials; Level 4 = principal/major arterials; Level 5 = TxDOT freeways/interstates.
    42→- Compute the **dedication delta** (future half-width minus existing half-width). Multiply by frontage length to get area lost. Flag if delta > 10 ft on any frontage or if total area lost > 10% of gross site.
    43→- Dedication is **roughly proportionate**; LDC § 25-6-23 requires a City-issued written proportionality determination signed by a City-retained PE before approval. Applicant-prepared SIF worksheets do not satisfy this requirement. Director may require less than full ASMP width but only via this memo.
    44→- Dedication is by recorded **street deed** (metes + bounds + surveyor-sealed sketch, processed through City Legal) or, where ROW is held as easement only, by plat. Recordation must precede site plan approval; instrument number must appear on plan callouts.
    45→- **TxDOT frontages (IH-35, US-290, SH-71, Parmer Lane, etc.)** carry long-term 400-ft ROW needs (200 ft from centerline). Either reserve up to 200 ft or obtain a TxDOT no-additional-dedication letter (LDC § 25-6-54(C)). TxDOT Approval Block required on the cover sheet when any work touches TxDOT ROW.
    46→- **Orange Line corridor**: up to 65 ft from centerline (130 ft total) reservation may apply. Streets to flag include Guadalupe, Lavaca, Congress Ave. Not codified in Bureau — verify against Project Connect System Plan map.
    47→- **Bicycle Priority Network**: streets on this network require All Ages and Abilities (AAA) facilities (Protected Bike Lanes, Shared Use Paths, or Neighborhood Bikeways per TCM 5.1.4); additional ROW beyond standard roadway width may be required.
    48→- **Waiver**: LDC § 25-6-81 — formal written waiver required if full dedication is infeasible; available when ≥ 15% of property is subject to ROW reservation. An informal "infeasible" note on plans does **not** satisfy. ATD usually conditions waiver on a recorded alternative easement (sidewalk or public access).
    49→- **IC math**: ROW pavement counts as IC; sidewalks in ROW or public easement are excluded (LDC § 25-8-63(C)(1)). On Hill Country Roadway sites, ROW > 60 ft from centerline counts in IC denominator (LDC § 25-2-1127), and 40% natural area is measured excluding dedicated ROW (LDC § 25-2-1025).
    50→
    51→### TIA threshold and likely findings
    52→
    53→- Threshold uses **unadjusted ITE daily trips** — no pass-by, internal capture, or TDM reductions for threshold determination. Only existing on-site occupied uses with documented occupancy may be subtracted.
    54→- < 2,000 trips: no study, but sub-threshold mitigation (sidewalks, signals, traffic calming, bike lanes, RRFB/PHB, urban trails, ROW, TDM) within ¼ mile (or ¾ mile to schools/bus stops/major roads) can still be required under LDC § 25-6-101(B).
    55→- 2,000–4,999 trips: **Transportation Assessment + TDM Plan** (LDC § 25-6-113; TCM 10.2.1).
    56→- ≥ 5,000 trips: **Full TIA + TDM Plan**.
    57→- All TIA work requires a **TDS-approved scope** signed by both the applicant's consultant and the TDS Lead Development Review Engineer *before* the study starts (TIA Guidelines § 4.3.2). Studies prepared without an approved scope will not be reviewed.
    58→- Approved TIAs are valid **5 years** from final memo date or assumed build-out, whichever is earlier (TCM 10.4.3). Plan trip-budgeting accordingly.
    59→- **TIA Compliance Letter** is a separate document from the TIA itself; if a prior TIA exists, expect a TIA Tracking Table on the cover sheet showing allowed/used/remaining VTDs and a 7-element compliance letter.
    60→- **NTA** triggers when project accesses a non-arterial street with ≥ 50% SF-5+ frontage within 1,500 ft AND adds ≥ 300 net new daily trips (or is a public K-12). TDS writes the memo; applicant submits 24-hr tube counts.
    61→- **Table 10-6** (TCM 10.4.4) sets nexus standards for required mitigations by category and study type — review before committing to off-site work.
    62→- **Fiscal surety** under LDC § 25-1-112 must be posted before site plan approval for any unbuilt TIA-required improvements; below-market cost estimates without director approval will be rejected.
    63→
    64→### Driveway and access management
    65→
    66→- **Driveway type by use + street level** (TCM 7.3.1–7.3.2): Type I (residential) is **prohibited on ASMP Level 3 or 4 streets** regardless of use. Multi-family > 4 units requires Type II.
    67→- **Max driveway width** (TCM 7.5.1.2, Table 7-2): Level 1 typical 20 ft (industrial 25 ft); Level 2 w/ 3-lane fire access 25 ft; high-capacity driveway serving a garage capped at 32 ft. Other Level 2/3/4 widths: verify against current TCM (Bureau data incomplete).
    68→- **Driveway count per frontage** is capped; **opposing-driveway offset** rules can force right-in/right-out only.
    69→- **Spacing minimums** from intersections, adjacent driveways, drainage inlets — confirm via TCM 7.6. Throat storage length per land use.
    70→- **Joint-use driveway** requires a recorded easement with maintenance assigned (TCM 7.6.4) — built into the title package.
    71→- **Hill Country Roadway** corridors (Loop 360 US-290W to US-183; RM 620 SH-71 to Anderson Mill; RM 2222 Highland Hills to RM 620; RM 2244 Loop 360 to SH-71; Southwest Parkway) impose extra access-spacing, grade, curve, and sight-distance restrictions (covered under guide 31).
    72→- **Curb return radii** per TCM Table 7-1; downtown / ERC / UNO / NBG have overlay-specific values.
    73→
    74→### Scenic Roadway constraints
    75→
    76→- **Scenic Roadway Sign District** (LDC § 25-10-81(3); LDC § 25-10-124) — applies to land within **1,000 ft of a Hill Country Roadway corridor** OR **200 ft of any of the 23 Scenic Roadways** enumerated in LDC § 25-10-7 (e.g., Barton Springs Rd, Lake Austin Blvd, MoPac, Loop 360, RM 2222, RM 2244, William Cannon, Riverside Dr, SH 130). Governs sign size, height, lighting, setback.
    77→- Historic and expressway sign districts override scenic per LDC § 25-10-82.
    78→- Note: the user prompt referenced LDC § 25-2-871 (scenic roadway). The bureau guides cite § 25-10-7 / § 25-10-81 / § 25-10-124 for the **sign district**, and Hill Country Roadway development standards at LDC § 25-2-1025 / § 25-2-1127 for the *development* envelope. Confirm the controlling section against current code before drafting findings.
    79→- For **Hill Country Roadway** sites the more material development constraints are the 40% natural-area requirement (excluding dedicated ROW; LDC § 25-2-1025), grade/cut-fill limits along the corridor, and ROW > 60 ft from centerline counting in IC denominator (LDC § 25-2-1127).
    80→
    81→### Sidewalk, transit, and bike obligations
    82→
    83→- **Sidewalk required on every street frontage** unless approved fee-in-lieu (LDC § 25-6-354; TCM 4.1.6). Minimum clear widths: Level 1 = 5 ft; Level 2 = 6 ft (constrained 5 ft w/ approval). Downtown Great Streets = 18 ft total streetscape zone; Core Transit Corridors = 15 ft total zone.
    84→- **Bicycle facilities** on the ASMP Bicycle Priority Network must be AAA-grade (Protected Bike Lane, Shared Use Path, or Neighborhood Bikeway per TCM 5.1.4). Planting-zone width: 8 ft (Level 2–3 recommended), 10 ft (Level 4 recommended), 6.5 ft constrained.
    85→- **Bus stop integration**: CapMetro coordination required where a stop fronts the site; floating bus stop platforms (where bike lane runs behind the stop) carry specific TCM dimensions.
    86→- **Bicycle parking** required citywide under LDC § 25-6-477 regardless of motor-vehicle parking; short-term + long-term split by use; TOD overlays add requirements.
    87→- **Accessible parking** is the only motor-vehicle parking minimum that survived the November 2023 elimination of general parking minimums (LDC §§ 25-6-471(B), 25-6-474(A)(3)). Calculated at 100% Appendix A → Building Code table; van-accessible 1 per 6 (IBC 1106.5).
    88→
    89→### Street Impact Fees
    90→
    91→- Applies to virtually all building-permit development (LDC § 25-6-662). Independent of TIA — a TIA waiver does *not* waive SIF.
    92→- **Assessed** at plat or building permit application; **collected** at building permit issuance (LDC § 25-6-663(B)). Plan notes stating SIF is paid at site plan approval are incorrect.
    93→- Process: applicant submits SIF Estimator Worksheet via ATD KNACK portal → TDS Engineering issues SIF Formal Calculation Memo → payment at each building permit.
    94→- SIF can be used as the proportionality measure under § 25-6-23.
    95→- Offset agreements available under § 25-6-669 for developer-constructed Roadway Capacity Plan improvements.
    96→- Required cover-sheet note: *"Development of structures that require a building permit within this Site Plan, or revisions thereof, are required to comply with the City of Austin Street Impact Fee Ordinances, as applicable, and must be paid upon completion of the building permit plan review for each building. Reference: LDC 25-6-662."*
    97→
    98→## Opportunities to evaluate
    99→
   100→- **TIA-driven public improvements**: TIAs frequently identify intersection improvements that the city or TxDOT may co-fund or accelerate; coordinate with TDS during scoping.
   101→- **Sub-threshold projects can structure SIF offsets** by constructing on-Roadway-Capacity-Plan improvements (LDC § 25-6-669) rather than paying full SIF.
   102→- **Fee-in-lieu of sidewalk** under LDC § 25-6-354 / TCM 4.1.6 — useful where physical sidewalk install conflicts with trees, drainage, or existing utilities.
   103→- **TIA waiver** under LDC § 25-6-117 — does not waive mitigation, but can streamline timeline if scope is genuinely limited.
   104→- **Cross-access / shared driveway** with neighboring sites reduces driveway count, can satisfy joint-use easement (TCM 7.6.4), and is preferred by ATD on arterials.
   105→- **Regulating plan bonuses**: ERC, NBG, and TOD districts include reduced parking maxima and active-edge incentives that can be leveraged in concept design.
   106→- **Project Connect / ETOD proximity** — ETOD-zoned sites (LDC § 25-2-182) carry density bonuses tied to transit corridor presence; verify against ETOD subdistrict layer.
   107→
   108→## Inputs needed from Phase 2
   109→
   110→- **transportation.md** — for each street frontage: existing ROW width (survey), ASMP Street Level + target half-width, Bicycle Priority Network status, AADT (TxDOT for state-maintained), functional class, posted speed, Project Connect / scenic / Hill Country flags.
   111→- **property-records.md** — recorded street deeds, existing access easements, joint-use driveway easements, vacated street documentation, prior ROW dedication instrument numbers.
   112→- **phase1-extraction/concept-plan-data.md** — proposed land use mix (with ITE codes), gross square footage / unit counts, proposed driveway locations + count, design vehicle (WB-50 vs. WB-62), parking garage proposed (high-capacity driveway?).
   113→- **zoning / overlays** — regulating plan membership (NBG, ERC, MLK TOD, Plaza Saltillo, Lamar/Justin Lane), Hill Country Roadway corridor flag, Scenic Roadway flag, UNO / NCCD overlays, ETOD subdistrict.
   114→- **adjacent_context** (surveyor `property_profile` + `adjacent_context`) — abutting ASMP/AMTP segments, neighbor zoning for NTA frontage test.
   115→
   116→## Output structure
   117→
   118→Standard discipline output shape; cite `references/phase3-disciplines.md`.
   119→
   120→## Severity heuristics
   121→
   122→| Finding | Severity |
   123→|---|---|
   124→| Future ROW dedication consumes > 10% of gross site OR > 15% of any one frontage's developable depth | `significant` |
   125→| Project triggers Full TIA (≥ 5,000 unadjusted trips) with likely off-site mitigation obligations | `significant` |
   126→| TxDOT frontage with unresolved 200-ft long-term ROW reservation (IH-35, US-290, SH-71, Parmer) | `significant` |
   127→| Orange Line / Project Connect corridor reservation plausibly applies (Guadalupe, Lavaca, Congress) | `significant` (flag for human verification) |
   128→| Project triggers Transportation Assessment (2,000–4,999 trips) with TDM Plan | `moderate` to `significant` |
   129→| Proposed driveway location conflicts with TCM 7.6 spacing or Type I prohibited on Level 3/4 | `moderate` |
   130→| NTA likely triggered (≥ 300 net new trips + residential frontage) | `moderate` |
   131→| Hill Country Roadway corridor frontage (Loop 360, RM 620/2222/2244, SW Parkway) | `moderate` |
   132→| Site within 200 ft of a § 25-10-7 Scenic Roadway (sign + character constraints) | `moderate` |
   133→| Bicycle Priority Network frontage requiring AAA facility ROW beyond standard | `moderate` |
   134→| Site requires sidewalk fee-in-lieu or shared-access agreement | `note` to `moderate` |
   135→| Adequate existing ROW + sub-2,000-trip use + no overlay frontage | `note` |
   136→
   137→## Common pitfalls
   138→
   139→- **Citing existing ROW instead of future ASMP ROW** when sizing setbacks or area calculations. The legal dedication obligation is from centerline to ASMP target half-width, not from the existing property line.
   140→- **Applying pass-by, internal-capture, or TDM reductions to TIA threshold trips.** Threshold determination uses *unadjusted* ITE rates only. Reductions can be claimed in the TIA itself, never in the determination.
   141→- **Treating SIF as paid at site plan approval.** SIF is **collected at building permit issuance** per LDC § 25-6-663(B). Cover sheet notes asserting otherwise are a checklist deficiency.
   142→- **Submitting applicant-engineer SIF worksheet as the § 25-6-23 proportionality determination.** The determination must be a City-issued memo signed by a City-retained PE.
   143→- **Starting TIA work before TDS-signed scope.** Studies prepared before scope approval will not be reviewed.
   144→- **Confusing functional class with jurisdictional ownership.** ASMP Level 5 = TxDOT; streets prefixed IH/US/SH = TxDOT-maintained. ASMP Level 4 includes service roads/ramps, which surveyor data flags as *not* highways.
   145→- **Missing Scenic Roadway Sign District** — applies up to 200 ft from any of 23 named roadways and 1,000 ft from Hill Country Roadway corridors. Easy to miss because the *sign* district lives in Chapter 25-10 rather than the transportation chapter.
   146→- **Confusing Scenic Roadway sign rules (Ch. 25-10) with Hill Country Roadway development rules (LDC §§ 25-2-1025, 25-2-1127).** Different overlays, different impacts — site can be in one but not the other.
   147→- **Citing 65 ft / 130 ft Orange Line reservation as a Bureau-codified requirement.** It is not in TCM or LDC; it comes from the Project Connect System Plan map. Always flag for external verification.
   148→- **Type I driveway proposed on a Level 3 or Level 4 street.** Always prohibited regardless of use (TCM 7.3.1.C).
   149→- **Plat used to dedicate easements** (sidewalk, sight distance, public access). Plat approval is not acceptance of dedication (LDC § 30-2-39); separate easement instruments using City templates are required.
   150→- **Assuming general motor-vehicle parking minimums still apply.** Austin eliminated minimums in November 2023; only accessible parking + bicycle parking minimums survive.
   151→- **Ignoring the 5-year TIA validity window.** Older TIAs need TDS written confirmation of continued validity or an updated study (TCM 10.4.3).

# Transportation Findings — 12713 Cinchring Ln

**Property:** 12713 Cinchring Ln, Austin, TX 78727 — Lot 12, Block M, Scofield Subdivision
**Proposed use:** Demolish existing SFR; build ground-up duplex (2 units)
**Lot:** ~7,840 sq ft (0.18 acres), SF-2 zoning
**Frontage:** Cinchring Ln (ASMP Level 1, local residential, City of Austin)

---

## Summary

- **No Traffic Impact Analysis (TIA) required.** The duplex generates approximately 10 net new daily trips, far below Austin's 2,000-trip TIA threshold. No TIA Determination Worksheet filing is necessary.
- **No ROW dedication anticipated.** Cinchring Ln is an ASMP Level 1 street with a 50-ft ROW standard; the existing platted ROW already meets this width, so no dedication delta exists.
- **Driveway permit required.** Demolition of the existing concrete drive and construction of a new driveway serving the duplex will require a driveway permit under TCM Section 7.
- **Sidewalk construction or fee-in-lieu likely required.** Austin requires a minimum 5-ft sidewalk along frontage on Level 1 streets. Existing sidewalk conditions on Cinchring Ln should be confirmed; if absent or substandard, the developer must construct or pay fee-in-lieu per LDC Section 25-6-354.
- **No scenic roadway, Hill Country Roadway, or Project Connect overlay constraints apply.** The site is well outside all designated scenic corridors, Hill Country Roadway corridors, and Project Connect rail reservation areas.

---

## Findings

### 1. TIA Not Required

| Field | Detail |
|---|---|
| **Severity** | `note` |
| **Citation** | LDC Section 25-6-111 through 25-6-117; TCM Section 10; TIA Guidelines Section 2 |
| **Finding** | The project replaces one single-family unit with a duplex (2 units), yielding a net increase of approximately 1 unit and roughly 9-10 net new daily trips (ITE Land Use 210/220, ~9.4 trips/unit). The TIA threshold is 2,000 unadjusted daily trips. The project is orders of magnitude below this threshold. The Neighborhood Traffic Analysis (NTA) trigger of 300 net new daily trips on a residential street is also not met. |
| **Implication** | No TIA, Transportation Assessment, TDM Plan, or NTA is required. No TDS coordination is needed for traffic study purposes. |
| **Recommended next step** | None required. No TIA Determination Worksheet filing necessary for a project of this scale. |

### 2. No ROW Dedication Required

| Field | Detail |
|---|---|
| **Severity** | `note` |
| **Citation** | LDC Section 25-6-51, 25-6-54; ASMP Street Network Table; TCM Section 2 |
| **Finding** | Cinchring Ln is classified as ASMP Level 1 with a 50-ft ROW standard. The existing platted ROW in the Scofield Subdivision meets this 50-ft standard. The dedication delta is zero. No street deed or plat-based dedication is anticipated. |
| **Implication** | The developer retains the full existing lot area; no buildable area is lost to future ROW dedication. Setbacks are measured from the existing property line. |
| **Recommended next step** | Confirm existing ROW width against the survey at site plan review. If any discrepancy is identified, the City would require dedication along the frontage as a condition of approval. |

### 3. Driveway Permit Required

| Field | Detail |
|---|---|
| **Severity** | `moderate` |
| **Citation** | TCM Section 7 (Driveways), specifically 7.3.1 (driveway types), 7.5.1.2 (width), 7.6 (spacing) |
| **Finding** | The existing concrete driveway will be demolished with the house. A new driveway serving the duplex must be permitted under TCM Section 7. On a Level 1 street, a Type I (residential) driveway is permitted. Maximum width is typically 20-24 ft for a two-way residential driveway. A single shared driveway serving both duplex units is the standard configuration and satisfies all spacing requirements. Minimum 30-ft setback from the nearest cross-street curb return applies. |
| **Implication** | The driveway permit is a standard requirement but must be coordinated with the building permit timeline. Driveway location must not conflict with TCM spacing standards or the existing 5-ft PUE along the lot line. |
| **Recommended next step** | Submit driveway permit application concurrent with building permit. Confirm driveway location relative to any opposing driveways across Cinchring Ln and adjacent lot driveways for offset compliance. |

### 4. Sidewalk Obligation Along Frontage

| Field | Detail |
|---|---|
| **Severity** | `moderate` |
| **Citation** | LDC Section 25-6-354 (fee-in-lieu); TCM Section 4.1.6; LDE Residential Review Guidelines (rev. November 2025) |
| **Finding** | Austin requires a minimum 5-ft clear-width sidewalk along all street frontages for new residential development on Level 1 streets. Whether Cinchring Ln currently has a sidewalk along the project frontage is not confirmed in the available data. If a sidewalk exists and meets current standards, no action is needed beyond maintaining it. If absent or substandard, the developer must either construct a compliant sidewalk or, if physical constraints exist (trees, drainage, utilities), apply for fee-in-lieu under LDC Section 25-6-354. |
| **Implication** | Sidewalk construction adds modest cost and must be coordinated with driveway placement and the 5-ft PUE. If heritage or protected trees are present in the ROW, fee-in-lieu may be the more practical path. |
| **Recommended next step** | Conduct a site visit or review aerial imagery to confirm existing sidewalk conditions along the Cinchring Ln frontage. If sidewalk construction is required, incorporate it into the civil site plan. If obstructions exist, pursue fee-in-lieu early in the permitting process. |

### 5. Street Impact Fee Applies

| Field | Detail |
|---|---|
| **Severity** | `note` |
| **Citation** | LDC Section 25-6-662, 25-6-663(B) |
| **Finding** | Street Impact Fees (SIF) apply to virtually all building-permit development in Austin, independent of TIA status. SIF is assessed at plat or building permit application and collected at building permit issuance. For a net increase of one dwelling unit, the fee will be modest but must be accounted for in the project budget. |
| **Implication** | SIF is payable at building permit issuance, not at site plan approval. The required cover-sheet note referencing LDC 25-6-662 must appear on plans. |
| **Recommended next step** | Submit SIF Estimator Worksheet via ATD KNACK portal to obtain the formal calculation memo prior to building permit application. Budget for SIF in development pro forma. |

### 6. No Scenic Roadway or Hill Country Roadway Overlay

| Field | Detail |
|---|---|
| **Severity** | `note` |
| **Citation** | LDC Section 25-10-7 (scenic roadways); LDC Section 25-10-81(3) (scenic roadway sign district); LDC Section 25-2-1025/25-2-1127 (Hill Country Roadway) |
| **Finding** | Cinchring Ln is not a designated scenic roadway. The site is not within 200 ft of any of the 23 enumerated scenic roadways (LDC Section 25-10-7), nor within 1,000 ft of a Hill Country Roadway corridor. Neither Scofield Ridge Pkwy nor the Parmer Ln segment in this area carries a scenic or Hill Country overlay. |
| **Implication** | No scenic roadway sign district constraints, no Hill Country Roadway development standards (40% natural area, grade/cut-fill limits), and no additional sign restrictions apply. |
| **Recommended next step** | None required. |

### 7. Limited Transit Access

| Field | Detail |
|---|---|
| **Severity** | `note` |
| **Citation** | CapMetro system map; Project Connect Orange Line planning documents |
| **Finding** | The site has limited transit access. The nearest bus service (CapMetro Routes 392 and 243) operates along Parmer Ln and Tech Ridge, approximately 1.0-2.0 miles away, with 30-60 minute headways. The Red Line commuter rail at Howard Station is approximately 2.5 miles east. The Project Connect Orange Line's planned northern extensions to Parmer/Tech Ridge are future-phase and have no construction timeline. The site is not within an ETOD subdistrict. |
| **Implication** | No transit-related development obligations, CapMetro coordination requirements, or bus stop integration work. The site is auto-dependent for practical purposes. No Project Connect ROW reservation applies. |
| **Recommended next step** | Informational only. No action required. |

### 8. No Bicycle Facility Construction Required

| Field | Detail |
|---|---|
| **Severity** | `note` |
| **Citation** | ASMP Bicycle Priority Network; TCM Section 5.1.4 |
| **Finding** | Cinchring Ln is not on the ASMP Bicycle Priority Network. As a low-speed (25 mph), low-volume Level 1 residential street, shared-lane (bicycle-with-traffic) operation is the applicable standard. No protected bike lane, shared-use path, or neighborhood bikeway construction is required. |
| **Implication** | No additional ROW beyond the standard roadway width is needed for bicycle facilities. No impact on site layout or buildable area. |
| **Recommended next step** | None required. Note that bicycle parking minimums under LDC Section 25-6-477 still apply citywide — verify required short-term and long-term bicycle parking counts for a duplex use. |

### 9. Parking Minimums — Cross-Reference

| Field | Detail |
|---|---|
| **Severity** | `note` |
| **Citation** | LDC Sections 25-6-471(B), 25-6-474(A)(3); cross-reference to ZLU discipline |
| **Finding** | Austin eliminated general motor-vehicle parking minimums in November 2023. Only accessible parking and bicycle parking minimums survive. For a 2-unit duplex, no minimum number of motor-vehicle parking spaces is required by city code. Accessible parking requirements apply per building code (Appendix A / IBC 1106.5) only if the project meets the threshold for required accessible spaces. |
| **Implication** | Parking is at the developer's discretion for unit marketability. Detailed parking analysis is covered in the ZLU discipline. |
| **Recommended next step** | See ZLU discipline findings for full parking analysis. Confirm bicycle parking requirements under LDC Section 25-6-477. |

---

## Open Questions for the Engineer

1. **Existing sidewalk conditions:** Does a sidewalk currently exist along the project's Cinchring Ln frontage? If so, what is its width and condition? This determines whether new construction, reconstruction, or fee-in-lieu is the appropriate path.

2. **Driveway configuration:** Will the duplex use a single shared driveway or two separate driveways? Confirm proposed driveway location(s) relative to opposing driveways and adjacent lot driveways for TCM Section 7.6 offset compliance.

3. **Survey-confirmed ROW width:** The research assumes the existing platted ROW meets the 50-ft Level 1 standard. Has the boundary survey confirmed the ROW width along the Cinchring Ln frontage, or is this assumption based on plat records alone?

4. **Heritage/protected trees in ROW:** Are there any heritage or protected trees within the ROW or along the property frontage that could constrain sidewalk construction or driveway placement?

5. **SIF estimate:** Has the SIF Estimator Worksheet been submitted to obtain the formal calculation memo? The net-new-unit increment is small, but the fee amount should be confirmed for the pro forma.
